t: Detect Pattern of Length M Repeated K or More Times - The Shift-by-M Streak Trick
o: We need some contiguous block of length m that repeats k times back-to-back inside arr. The brute-force reading slides a window of length m*k over the array and verifies the k-1 following m-blocks against the first at every start. A slicker view: a block repeats exactly when the array agrees with its own shift by m across k-1 consecutive aligned positions, i.e. arr[i] = arr[i-m] holds for a stretch of (k-1)*m consecutive indices. Counting that streak in one pass detects every repetition. The samples confirm it: [1,2,4,4,4,4] with m=1,k=3 builds a streak of 3, while [1,2,1,2,1,3] with m=2,k=3 peaks at 3, short of the required 4.
k: A block of length m repeating k times is equivalent to arr[i] = arr[i-m] holding along (k-1)*m consecutive positions.
A running streak counter over the shift-by-m comparison checks the whole array in O(n) time and O(1) space.
Fail fast when m*k exceeds arr.length - no pattern can physically fit.

a.i: Translate the definition directly: try each start position where a length-m*k segment fits, and compare each of the k-1 subsequent m-blocks against the first block. It wastes effort re-comparing overlapping segments, but with arr.length at most 100 the quadratic-ish cost is irrelevant, making this a perfectly respectable submission and the clearest baseline to present first.
s: For each start from 0 while start + m*k fits in the array:
Compare block j (for j = 1..k-1) cell-by-cell against block 0.
Return true as soon as all comparisons for some start succeed.
Return false if every start fails.
a.t: O(n * m * k) - up to n candidate starts, each verified against m*(k-1) cells.
a.sp: O(1) - only loop indices and flags.

a.i: Key off the equivalence between block repetition and self-alignment under a shift of m. Sweep i from m to the end, extending a streak when arr[i] equals arr[i-m] and resetting it to zero on any mismatch. Once the streak reaches (k-1)*m, the last k aligned blocks agree pairwise in cascade, which is precisely a pattern repeated k times. One comparison per index, no extra memory, and the early bail-out m*k > n avoids even scanning hopeless inputs.
s: If m * k exceeds the array length, return false immediately.
Iterate i from m to n-1 comparing arr[i] with arr[i-m].
Grow the streak on a match; reset it to 0 on a mismatch.
Return true the moment the streak reaches (k-1)*m; otherwise return false.
a.t: O(n) - exactly one comparison per array index.

w: Name the brute force in one sentence, then implement the streak scan - same conceptual load, linear time, minimal surface area for bugs. The classic off-by-one is the threshold: you need (k-1)*m matched adjacent pairs, not k*m, since k repetitions create only k-1 seams. Another pitfall is resetting the streak on the wrong condition - it must reset per position, not per block. Worth stating: k >= 2 by the constraints, so the target is always positive. Follow-ups: return the longest repeating block, tolerate one mismatch per period (keep a mismatch budget inside the streak), or detect such patterns in a stream with limited memory.
